red_flags: Did not progress the quote to landlord approval, which is what the human did
Asked the contractor to resend a quote that had already arrived, adding delay and noise
Added a profile fact about contractor responsiveness that was not needed
reasoning: The reference shows the operator forwarded the quote to the landlord for approval. The agent saw only a one-line summary of the quote, with no figures, and the landlord contact record was empty. So it could not send an approval request without inventing amounts. Its response was cautious and honest. It told the contractor not to start work, put the ticket on hold, and escalated to ops to find the original email, add landlord details and deal with the duplicate ticket. It committed no landlord money, invented no figures and used no future information. It did not reach the main outcome, which was to get the quote to the landlord for approval. Asking the contractor to resend a quote that had already arrived was probably unnecessary and slows the case. The safe escalation keeps this at a partial rather than a fail.
